newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK PRESIDENT SEEN TWINNING REFERENDA NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK PRESIDENT SEEN TWINNING REFERENDA NEXT WEEK.

text.p: Slovak President Michal Kovac will decide next week on whether to twin a referendum on direct presidential elections with one on the country's membership in NATO, a presidential spokesman said on Friday.
"So far the President has been in favour of linking these two (referenda) together," Vladimir Stefko told Reuters.
"The President will make a final decision on dates of these referenda at the beginning of the next week, when he is expected to receive the petition lists," he added.
Meciar's ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) spearheaded a campaign for a referendum on the country's possible entry into NATO. Earlier this month parliament approved such a vote.
Meanwhile, Slovakia's opposition said it had collected more than 350,000 signatures needed to force a referendum on the direct election of the President.
The petitioners have said they would like the referendum on presidential elections to be held on the same day as the NATO plebiscite.
Earlier this week, Meciar, an avowed political foe of Kovac, rejected the twinning of the referenda saying it would be unreasonable. "These (two) things are unequal and unbalanced," Meciar said.

He has also rejected the referendum on direct presidential elections itself, hinting that his government would ask the country's Constitutional Court for ruling on whether it was possible to change the constitution by a referendum.

The governing coalition, led by HZDS, and the opposition appear unable to agree on a common presidential candidate and neither is able to garner the three-fifths majority necessary in the 150-seat house to push through their own choice in a vote shceduled for March 1998.

If such a stalemate occurs, Meciar would assume presidential powers until a new parliament is elected at elections planned for the autumn of 1998, when the body would again have to propose a presidential candidate.
